summary: Geshe Lhakdor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery. He served as Director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives from 2005.

Geshe Lhundup Sopa (1923–2014) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Gaden Chokhor and Sera Jey under Geshe Lhundrup Tabkhe and others. He served as Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and founded the Deer Park Buddhist Center in 1976.

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin (1921–2004) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery, earning his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

Geshe Losang Chödar is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he is attested as Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics and held a post at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.
Geshe Ngawang Nyima (1907–1990) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as Abbot of Drepung Gomang Monastery and held posts at Drepung Monastery and Leiden University.

Geshe Ngawang Samten (b. 1956) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and Ganden Shartse Monastery, and served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from ~1988 to 2021.
Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held posts at Tibet House, New Delhi, where he is attested as Librarian from 1987 to 1992 and attested in 2004.
Geshe Palden Drakpa is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and is attested as Librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, in 1988.

Geshe Rabten (1920–1986) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Trijang Rinpoche, taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1969–1974), and founded Rabten Choeling in 1977.

Geshe Sonam Rinchen (1933–2013) was a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. In 1978, he became a resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Geshe Tashi Tsering (b. 1958) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries under teachers including Geshe Thubten Rinchen. He served as a teacher at Kopan Monastery (~1992–1994) and resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre from 1994.

Geshe Tenzin Dhargye (b. 1968) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studying at Sera Monastery, Gyume Tantric College, and under Ling Rinpoche. He taught at Sera, Gyume, and the University of Virginia, and became Director of Tibetzentrum Österreich in 2008.
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned Geshe degrees studying at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

Geshe Wangyal (1901–1983) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Drepung Monastery under Agvan Dorzhiev. He taught at Columbia University (~1967–1974) and founded the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, serving there from ~1958 to 1983.

Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe (b. 1930) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held posts as a scholar at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested between 1991 and 2019.

Geshe Yeshe Tobden (1926–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from ~1967 to 1971.
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin completed his studies under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gessho Sasaki (1875–1926) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as lecturer, professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925) at Otani University, and founded the Eastern Buddhist Society in 1921.

Ghanshyam Sharma (b. 1958) is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held a post at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (attested 1998) and became a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales in 2012.

Gheorghe Bogdan-Duică (1866–1934) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Jena, the University of Vienna, and the University of Bucharest, and became Professor of Modern Romanian Literature at Babeș-Bolyai University in 1919.
